reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Program creation and council safety rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 2, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3). Covers creation of the dam and reservoir safety program in the department of natural resources and council authority to promulgate rules, regulations, guidelines, and standards on determining danger to public safety, life, or property, qualified by director approval.

headings.title: Employment of chief engineer and assistants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers the duty of the director of the department of natural resources to employ an experienced professional engineer as chief engineer and assistants to administer program activities.

headings.title: Merit-system selection of chief engineer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 2 by specifying selection under the state merit system based on professional experience directly related to dam and reservoir design and construction.

headings.title: Permanent public records of findings, opinions, and orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers keeping findings, opinions, and orders of both the council and the chief engineer as permanent public records in department of natural resources offices. Revised during review to include opinions alongside findings and orders.

headings.title: Rule effectiveness under section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Preserves the exact cross-reference conditioning effectiveness of any rule or portion of a rule under sections 236.400 to 236.500 on promulgation pursuant to section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 2, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3) and verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, subsection count/numbering, and all bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked DNR program creation, director-approved council rulemaking, chief engineer employment vs. merit-system selection, permanent records, and the exact section 536.024 rulemaking effectiveness cross-reference. Revised subsection 4 title to include 'opinions' alongside findings and orders; retained subsections 1-3 and 5.

headings.title: Council creation, domicile, and appointment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, catchline (*236.410), and notes (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 3, A.L. 1992 H.B. 1634, A.L. 2013 H.B. 28 merged with H.B. 650; dual effective dates 8-28-13 for H.B. 28 and 10-11-13 for H.B. 650 after July 12, 2013 veto and September 11, 2013 override under § 21.250). Covers creating the seven-member Dam and Reservoir Safety Council domiciled in the department of natural resources, the four-member political party cap, and gubernatorial appointment with senate advice and consent.

headings.title: Member qualifications, terms, meetings, expenses, and annual report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and dual-effective-date/merged-enactment notes (H.B. 28 and H.B. 650 veto override). Covers member training/experience and seat composition (retaining source phrasing "one of whom shall be earthmoving contractors" and "three shall be from each of the three United States congressional districts in this state with the highest number of dams"), two-year terms with historical initial one-year exception, vacancies and removal for cause, annual election of chairman and vice chairman, quarterly and special meetings, four-member quorum and majority vote, travel/subsistence-only expense reimbursement ("compensations" in source), and annual report to the general assembly by December 31.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections, catchline (*236.410), and all history and effective-date notes (A.L. 2013 H.B. 28 merged with H.B. 650; dual effective dates 8-28-13 for H.B. 28 and 10-11-13 for H.B. 650 following July 12, 2013 veto and September 11, 2013 override under § 21.250), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Verified seven-member composition, four-member political party cap, initial one-year term exception, quorum/voting, travel-and-subsistence-only expenses, December 31 annual report, and source phrasing ('earthmoving contractors', 'three shall be from each of the three United States congressional districts', 'compensations'). Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Rule adoption, violation consequences, and hearing notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 4, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3). Covers council adoption of general technological guidelines, standards, rules, and regulations after a public meeting and subject to director approval, states that violations constitute violations of sections 236.400 to 236.500 permitting permit revocation, suspension, or refusal, and requires a public hearing with thirty days prior notice and chapter 536 publication before adoption, amendment, or repeal.

headings.title: Hearing participation, written comments, and action notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers opportunity to be heard upon written request addressed to the chief engineer at least seven days before the hearing (and for others if convenient), seven-day post-hearing written statements, optional council solicitation of written views, and written notice of council action to participants and requesters.

headings.title: Permit decisions and delegation to chief engineer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers council approval or denial of construction or registration permit applications after chief engineer recommendations, and permissive delegation of that authority to the chief engineer subject to council appeal under section 236.425(2).

headings.title: Director approval, chapter 536 compliance, and council vote
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Conditions force and effect of any adopted, amended, or repealed standard, rule, regulation, or guideline on written director approval and chapter 536 compliance, and requires an affirmative vote of at least four council members for adoption.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 4, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked director-approval and chapter 536 prerequisites, 30-day public hearing notice, 7-day pre- and post-hearing participation windows, permissive delegation to the chief engineer subject to section 236.425(2) appeal, and the four-member council adoption vote. Retained all four drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Chief engineer recommendations, investigations, inspections, and search warrants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and notes (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 6; original-rolls note `*Words "To make" appear in original rolls.` on "Making*" in subdivision (2)). Covers administering sections 236.400 to 236.500 by recommending general technological guidelines without detailed technical specifications (effective only after council adoption, director approval, and section 236.415(1) notice), making permit recommendations, conducting investigations and hearings, and entering public or private premises after reasonable prior notice (or without notice in emergencies) with probable-cause restricted search warrants. Revised during review to reflect guideline and permit recommendations in subdivisions (1) and (2).

headings.title: Council review of chief engineer permit rejections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers the council duty to meet with or hear the appeal of a permit applicant and representative upon request when the chief engineer has rejected an application for a construction, safety, or registration permit.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions (1)-(4) and all notes (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 6; original-rolls footnote `*Words "To make" appear in original rolls.` on `Making*` in subsection 1(2)) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked prohibition on detailed technical specifications, section 236.415(1) notice condition, emergency no-notice inspection exception, probable-cause restricted search warrants, and council review of rejected permit applications. Revised subsection 1 title to explicitly reflect guideline and permit recommendations in subdivisions (1)-(2); retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Construction permit requirement before dam work
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 8). Covers the owner requirement to apply to the council and obtain a construction permit upon satisfying sections 236.400 to 236.500 and adopted rules before commencing construction, alteration, enlargement, reduction, or removal of a dam or reservoir.

headings.title: Engineering seal, design report, and permit plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers required seal and signature of an experienced Missouri-registered professional engineer or qualified state/federal conservation, irrigation, or wildlife agency engineering division, together with the design report, plans, and specifications.

headings.title: Builder, owner, and affected-person consultation with chief engineer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. States permissive authority for any dam builder, owner, area resident or property owner, or person whose safety may be affected to consult with the chief engineer. Revised during review to include builders and owners rather than narrowing parties to affected persons.

headings.title: Construction permit review timeline and approval criteria
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers the forty-five-day council action period after application receipt or completion of hearings (whichever is later) and issuance standards based on statutory/regulatory compliance and design adequacy for public safety, life, and property.

headings.title: Grounds for rejecting construction permit applications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 4 by specifying permissive council grounds, upon chief engineer recommendation, to reject an application for insufficient safety information, danger to public safety, life, or property, or noncompliance with sections 236.400 to 236.500 and rules.

headings.title: Agricultural dam exemption and change in use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers the landowner exemption from sections 236.400 to 236.500 for dams or reservoirs used primarily for agricultural purposes, and loss of the exemption if the council with chief engineer advice determines the primary use changes.

headings.title: Conservation and irrigation dam exemption and plan filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 6 by covering the section-only exemption for dams designed and monitored by qualified soil/water conservation, irrigation, or wildlife conservation engineers, qualified by mandatory prior plan filing and completion amended-plan filing for significant deviations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all seven subsections and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 8) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked Missouri PE and qualified conservation/irrigation/wildlife agency engineering seal requirements, 45-day review timeline, permissive rejection grounds, full sections 236.400 to 236.500 agricultural dam exemption (including change-in-use loss), and section-only conservation/irrigation/wildlife exemption with mandatory prior and amended plan filing. Revised subsection 3 title to include builders and owners alongside affected persons; retained subsections 1-2 and 4-7.

headings.title: Completion notice and safety permit application
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 9). Covers owner notification upon completing construction, alteration, enlargement, or reduction with an experienced professional engineer seal and signature, accompanying safety permit application, and requirement to obtain a safety permit.

headings.title: Safety permit issuance, denial, revisions, and conditions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers issuance upon complete application and engineer certification, permissive denial for violations, safety showing required for substantial revisions, and council authority to attach safety conditions and compliance schedules no more stringent than the construction permit.

headings.title: Registration permit schedule and standards for existing dams
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Retains the archived September 28, 1979 existence date and four-year (50 to 70 feet) and six-year (up to 50 feet) registration permit deadlines, plus compliance determination standards prior to council issuance.

headings.title: Registration permit applications, certifications, and denial
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 3 by detailing DNR application forms for pre-September 28, 1979 dams, inspection and defect-correction certifications by an experienced engineer or qualified state/federal agency, issuance upon receipt, and permissive denial for noncompliance with recommendations.

headings.title: Compliance conditions on registration permits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers permissive council authority, upon chief engineer recommendations, to attach conditions to registration permits for dams completed prior to the effective date of construction permit requirements.

headings.title: Final approval for dam removal and violation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers council issuance of final approval after owner notification and professional engineer certification that removal complied with the construction permit, and makes failure to obtain final approval a violation of sections 236.400 to 236.500.

headings.title: Safety permits for agency-monitored conservation and irrigation dams
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Covers issuance of safety permits for dams designed and monitored by state or federal soil/water conservation, irrigation, or wildlife conservation agencies, conditioned on filing agency conformance and maintenance statements at completion, at intervals of five years or less, and with each renewal. Revised during review to include irrigation dams alongside conservation dams.

headings.title: Safety and registration permit renewal procedure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Covers renewal application at least sixty days before expiration, chief engineer inspection/compliance review, forty-five-day renewal issuance unless defects or noncompliance exist, and optional council requirement for engineer or agency maintenance certification.

headings.title: Barriers or impoundments becoming regulated dams or reservoirs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Brings any barrier or water impoundment that becomes a defined dam or reservoir through alteration or enlargement under sections 236.400 to 236.500. Revised during review to cover both barriers and impoundments becoming regulated dams or reservoirs without omitting enlargement.

headings.title: Failure to obtain or comply with permit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Declares failure to obtain and comply with a permit required in section 236.440 a violation of sections 236.400 to 236.500.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all ten subsections and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 9) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked completion notice, safety permit issuance/denial/conditions, archived September 28, 1979 registration permit deadlines (four- and six-year height tiers) and certifications, dam-removal final approval, five-year agency statements, 60-day renewal application / 45-day issuance procedure, regulated-dam threshold through alteration or enlargement, and statutory violation clauses. Revised subsection 7 title to include irrigation dams and subsection 9 title to cover both barriers and impoundments becoming regulated dams or reservoirs without omitting enlargement; retained subsections 1-6, 8, and 10.

headings.title: Permit suspension, alteration or removal, and cost recovery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 10). Covers mandatory permit suspension when a dam or reservoir threatens public safety, life, property, or its own safety, reinstatement conditions at owner expense, permissive council authority to require owner removal, and state alteration or removal with cost recovery under section 236.450 if the owner refuses or neglects to act.

headings.title: Refusal to alter or remove and permit revocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by making owner refusal to alter or remove a threatening dam or reservoir as directed a statutory and permit violation triggering enforcement provisions and permit revocation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 10) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked mandatory permit suspension on safety threats, owner-expense reinstatement conditions, permissive removal orders, state alteration/removal with section 236.450 cost recovery, and separate violation/revocation consequences for owner refusal in subsection 2. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Sworn testimony, stenographic recording, and transcripts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 15). Covers taking public-hearing testimony under oath before the council or chair-appointed hearing officer, stenographic recording, and transcript availability upon payment of the usual charge.

headings.title: Hearing notices, section 536.077 subpoenas, and civil discovery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers issuance of hearing notices and subpoenas in the council name by any council member or hearing officer, subpoena issuance and enforcement under section 536.077, and application of civil discovery rules.

headings.title: Four-member panel for rulemaking hearings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 4 by requiring hearings to approve, amend, or repeal guidelines, standards, or rules and regulations to be held before at least four council members.

headings.title: Presiding officers and recommendations in other hearings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 3 by permitting non-rulemaking hearings before one designated council member or a Missouri-bar hearing officer appointed by the chair, covering presiding duties, admissibility rulings, recommended findings of fact, and optional recommended conclusions of law.

headings.title: Approval of final council orders and record review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 15; original-rolls note `*Word "of" appears in original rolls.` on "final order or* determination"). Covers required written approval by at least four council members for final orders, determinations, or actions, and the prerequisite that non-attending approving members review all exhibits and read the entire transcript.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections and all notes (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 15; original-rolls footnote `*Word "of" appears in original rolls.` on `final order or* determination` in subsection 5) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked sworn stenographic testimony, exact section 536.077 subpoena and civil discovery provisions, four-member rulemaking panel vs. single-member or Missouri-bar hearing officer in other hearings, and four-member written approval with full exhibit/transcript review for non-attending members. Retained all five drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Judicial review under chapter 536 and exhaustion requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 17). Covers chapter 536 judicial review of final decisions, orders, actions, or determinations under sections 236.400 to 236.500, conditioned on exhaustion of all administrative remedies.

headings.title: Court review of rule validity under section 536.050
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by specifying the standard and record for suits filed under section 536.050 challenging the validity and reasonableness of adopted standards, rules, guidelines, and regulations, including permissive authority to hear additional evidence.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 17) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked chapter 536 judicial review conditioned on administrative-remedy exhaustion in subsection 1 and section 536.050 rule-validity record review with permissive additional evidence in subsection 2. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Subpoenas, document production, and court enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 20). Covers chief engineer and council authority to subpoena witnesses and compel books, papers, documents, or data in hearings, enforcement proceedings, or alleged chapter violations (to the extent consistent with chapter 491), and circuit court enforcement requested through the attorney general or prosecuting attorney.

headings.title: Injunctions, daily penalties after notice, and venue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers council requests to the attorney general or prosecuting attorney to sue in the state name for injunctive relief or, after written violation notice and reasonable time to correct, penalties up to $1,000 per day, together with venue options.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 20) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked chapter 491 consistency limitation on subpoenas/document compulsion, AG/prosecuting attorney circuit court enforcement, injunctive relief, written-notice and reasonable-correction prerequisite before daily penalties up to $1,000, and venue options. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for willful statutory violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 21). Covers misdemeanor classification and fine/jail penalty range ($500 to $10,000, 30 days to 1 year county jail, or both) for willful violations of sections 236.400 to 236.500.

headings.title: Each day of continuing violation as separate offense
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Provides that each day a continuing violation persists constitutes a separate and distinct offense.

headings.title: Willfully obstructing or resisting council or chief engineer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Distinguished from subsections 1 and 4 by criminalizing willful obstruction, hindrance, prevention, or resistance against the council, chief engineer, or their agents/employees performing duties under sections 236.400 to 236.500 and rules, punished under subsection 1.

headings.title: Willful owner violations of permit requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Distinguished from subsections 1 and 3 by specifically targeting owners who willfully construct, repair, alter, or remove a dam or reservoir without or in violation of a construction permit, or willfully violate safety or registration permit requirements, punished under subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history note (L. 1979 H.B. 603 § 21) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked willful mens rea across subsections 1, 3, and 4, misdemeanor fine/jail range ($500-$10,000; 30 days-1 year), separate daily continuing-violation offenses, obstruction/resistance of council/chief engineer duties, and owner-specific permit violations. Retained all four drafted titles as accurate.
